description: Unique synthetic patient alphanumeric identification code
Patient biological age in completed chronological years at examination
Biological sex / self-reported gender of the patient
Primary vocational category / occupational environment
allowed_values: Office / Desk Worker, Manual Laborer / Construction, Driver / Transport, Healthcare Professional, Teacher / Academic, Farmer / Agricultural, Retired / Elderly, Student, Homemaker, Sales / Retail

description: Clinical diagnosis or self-reported history of diabetes mellitus (Type 1 or 2)
Documented medical history of systemic arterial hypertension
Presence of major ocular disease in first-degree biological relatives (e.g., glaucoma, cataract, retinal dystrophy, severe myopia)
Surgical history involving either eye (e.g., cataract extraction, LASIK/PRK, trabeculectomy, retinal laser photocoagulation)
History of mechanical, blunt, sharp, or chemical trauma to ocular tissues
Current active or regular use of soft, rigid gas permeable, or cosmetic contact lenses
Lifetime tobacco cigarette smoking classification status
Subjective complaint of decreased visual clarity, fuzziness, or loss of sharpness at near or distance
Perception of moving dark specks, cobwebs, strings, or spots drifting across the visual field (vitreous floaters/hemorrhage)
Ocular discomfort, deep ache, retrobulbar pain, or sharp stinging sensation
Hyperemia of conjunctival, episcleral, or ciliary vasculature ('pink/red eye')
Pruritus or tickling sensation of the ocular surface, canthi, or lid margins
Sensation of insufficient tear lubrication, burning, scratchiness, or desiccated ocular surface
Epiphora or hyperlacrimation caused by reflex irritation or lacrimal drainage impairment
Diplopia: seeing two overlapping or separated images of a single object (monocular or binocular)
Photopsia: perceived streaks, lightning arcs, or flashes of light in the peripheral visual field
Photophobia or glare sensitivity provoked by normal indoor or outdoor light levels
Nyctalopia: impaired visual contrast, glare, or subnormal dark adaptation in mesopic or scotopic illumination
Edema of periorbital tissues, eyelids, or conjunctival chemosis
Cephalea, brow ache, temple pressure, or frontal asthenopic headache associated with eye strain or IOP changes
Mucopurulent, purulent, serous, or crusting exudate accumulating on eyelids, lashes, or canthi
Feeling of sand, grit, glass, or an eyelash lodged under the eyelid or on the corneal surface
Estimated elapsed duration in days from symptom onset to current clinical triage (0 if asymptomatic)
Temporal nature and speed of symptom manifestation
Patient-reported subjective overall intensity of presenting ocular symptoms
Anatomical laterality of the presenting ocular complaints or signs
Intraocular pressure (IOP) of the left eye measured via tonometry (Goldmann or non-contact); missing if deferred/omitted
Intraocular pressure (IOP) of the right eye measured via tonometry (Goldmann or non-contact); missing if deferred/omitted
Best-measured or presenting visual acuity of the left eye expressed on the standardized LogMAR continuous scale (0.00 = 20/20 standard normal; 1.00 = 20/200; higher values indicate worse acuity)
Best-measured or presenting visual acuity of the right eye expressed on the standardized LogMAR continuous scale (0.00 = 20/20 standard normal; 1.00 = 20/200; higher values indicate worse acuity)
Vertical optic nerve head cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) of the left eye evaluated via fundoscopy / slit lamp biomicroscopy; missing if dilated exam not indicated/performed
Vertical optic nerve head cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) of the right eye evaluated via fundoscopy / slit lamp biomicroscopy; missing if dilated exam not indicated/performed
Specific positive family history of open-angle or angle-closure glaucoma in direct biological relatives
Prior documented medical diagnosis of glaucoma or ongoing prescription for ocular hypotensive drops
Target clinical diagnostic classification assigned based on comprehensive multi-feature synthetic assessment
allowed_values: Normal, Glaucoma, Cataract, Diabetic_Retinopathy, Conjunctivitis, Dry_Eye_Disease, Refractive_Error
